note.explanation: Air pollution is harmful material in the air. It can harm people, other living things and the environment. Pollutants include gases such as carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide, as well as particles such as dust and smoke.
examples: Carbon monoxide is poisonous and can stop blood from carrying the oxygen the body needs.
Smog can reduce the carbon dioxide plants absorb during photosynthesis, inhibiting their growth.
note.checkAnswer: Smog can reduce the carbon dioxide plants absorb during photosynthesis, inhibiting their growth.
note.simple: Air pollution means harmful substances in the air. Some are gases; others are tiny particles. They can make people ill and harm plants and the environment.
note.checkQuestion: How can smog affect the growth of plants?
note.title: Air Pollutants
steps: An air pollutant is a substance in the air that harms human health or quality of life.
The main pollutants include carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen and sulphur, hydrocarbons, particulates and ozone.
Burning fossil fuels is a major source of air pollution.
Smog forms when smoke in the atmosphere mixes with fog in winter.
Pollutants can cause breathing problems, acid rain, global warming and harm to plants.
note.answer: Smog reduces the carbon dioxide absorbed during photosynthesis, so it inhibits plant growth.

options: A substance in air that adversely affects health or quality of life
Any substance that improves air quality
Only a solid particle suspended in air
A gas that is always harmless
mcqs.stem: Which description best defines an air pollutant?
rationales: This is the definition given in the section.
A substance that improves air quality is not a pollutant by this definition.
Air pollutants may be solid, liquid or gas, not only solid particles.
Air pollutants are harmful; they are not necessarily harmless gases.

options: One part of pollutant per million parts of the mixture
One million parts of pollutant per one part of mixture
One part of pollutant per thousand parts of the mixture
One part of pollutant per hundred parts of the mixture
mcqs.stem: What does a concentration of one ppm mean?
rationales: One ppm means one part of pollutant per million parts of the mixture.
This reverses the pollutant and mixture quantities.
One part per thousand is not one ppm.
One part per hundred is not one ppm.

options: Complete and incomplete combustion of fossil fuels
Photosynthesis in plants
Mixing of smoke with fog
Absorption of carbon dioxide by plants
mcqs.stem: Which activity is described as a major cause of air pollution?
rationales: The section identifies complete and incomplete fossil-fuel combustion as the major human activity causing pollution.
Photosynthesis absorbs carbon dioxide rather than being identified as a major source of air pollution.
Smoke mixed with fog forms smog; it is not the major activity identified as the source of most pollution.
Plants absorbing carbon dioxide is not a major source of air pollution.

options: Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, NOₓ, SOₓ, methane, ash, smoke and suspended particles
Only oxygen and nitrogen
Only ozone and water vapour
Only dust and pollen
mcqs.stem: Which group of pollutants can be produced by burning fossil fuels?
rationales: The section lists these gases and particles as products of fossil-fuel burning.
Oxygen and nitrogen alone are not the listed pollutants produced by burning fossil fuels.
This list leaves out the pollutants named in the section and adds water vapour.
Dust and pollen are examples of particulates, but this is not the full group described.

options: Heat and sunlight cause a reaction between NOₓ and volatile organic compounds
Smoke mixes with fog
Methane is released by decomposition of vegetation
Sulphur dioxide dissolves in rain
mcqs.stem: According to the section, how is ozone formed?
rationales: The section says heat and sunlight cause a chemical reaction between NOₓ and volatile organic compounds.
Smoke mixing with fog forms smog, not ozone.
Decomposition of vegetation releases methane; it is not the stated ozone-forming process.
Sulphur dioxide and rain are associated with acid rain, not the stated formation of ozone.

options: Smoke in the atmosphere mixes with fog
Ozone mixes with methane
Dust mixes with rainwater
Carbon dioxide mixes with sunlight
mcqs.stem: How does the section describe the formation of winter smog?
rationales: The section defines winter smog as smoke in the atmosphere mixed with fog.
Ozone and methane are not described as forming smog by mixing.
Dust and rainwater are not the stated components of smog.
Carbon dioxide and sunlight are not the stated components of smog.

options: It can stop red blood cells from carrying oxygen needed by the body
It makes clothes dirty and reduces visibility
It causes ice caps to melt by increasing global warming
It reduces the amount of carbon dioxide plants absorb
mcqs.stem: Which harmful effect is associated with carbon monoxide in the section?
rationales: Carbon monoxide is poisonous and stops red blood cells from carrying the oxygen the body needs.
Dirty clothes and reduced visibility are effects of particulate matter.
Increased global warming and melting ice caps are described as effects of higher carbon dioxide levels.
Reduced carbon dioxide absorption by plants is linked to smog.

options: Eye irritation and breathing difficulties
Only increased oxygen in the blood
Improved visibility
Faster growth of plants
mcqs.stem: Which effects of particulate matter are stated in the section?
rationales: Particulate matter can irritate the eyes and cause severe breathing problems, particularly for people with asthma.
The section does not say particulate matter increases oxygen in the blood.
Particulate matter produces haze and reduces visibility.
The section does not describe particulate matter as speeding plant growth.

written.text: How does air pollution affect plants?
written.finalAnswer: Smog inhibits the growth of plants by reducing the amount of carbon dioxide absorbed during photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Identifying smog connects the answer to the section's stated effect.
rubric.description: Identify smog as harmful to plants.
rubric.how: State that smog affects or inhibits plant growth.

rubric.why: The section explains the effect through reduced carbon dioxide absorption during photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Say that smog reduces the carbon dioxide absorbed during photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Smog reduces the amount of carbon dioxide absorbed by plants during photosynthesis.
Therefore, it inhibits the growth of plants.

written.text: How is particulate matter released in the atmosphere?
written.finalAnswer: Particulate matter is released by burning fossil fuels, and it can also enter the air through natural processes such as volcanic eruptions.

rubric.why: Fossil-fuel burning is a major source of pollutants, including ash, smoke and suspended particles.
rubric.how: State that burning fossil fuels releases particles.

rubric.why: The section also names volcanic eruptions as a natural source of particulates.
rubric.how: Give volcanic eruptions as an example.

modelAnswer: Burning fossil fuels releases ash, smoke and suspended particles into the air.
Natural processes such as volcanic eruptions also release particulates.

written.text: Which gas is more poisonous, CO₂ or CO?
written.finalAnswer: CO is more poisonous than CO₂.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the more poisonous gas.
rubric.how: Write CO or carbon monoxide.

rubric.why: A comparison makes clear which gas is more poisonous.
rubric.how: State that CO is more poisonous than CO₂.

modelAnswer: CO is more poisonous than CO₂.

written.text: In what way sulphur present in fossil fuels becomes dangerous?
written.finalAnswer: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur forms oxides of sulphur, which irritate the eyes, cause breathing difficulties and acid rain.

rubric.why: The harmful form is the oxides of sulphur produced when fuel burns.
rubric.how: State that burning produces oxides of sulphur.

rubric.why: Acid rain is one of the dangers of sulphur oxides given in the section.
rubric.how: Name acid rain or the breathing and eye effects.

modelAnswer: When fossil fuels containing sulphur are burnt, oxides of sulphur are produced.
These oxides irritate the eyes, cause breathing difficulties and cause acid rain.

written.text: Percentage of CO₂ in air is only 0.04%. Then how does it become harmful for the ecosystem?
written.finalAnswer: Even though CO₂ is only 0.04% of air, higher levels lead to increased global warming. This can melt ice caps, warm oceans and raise sea levels, and can cause extreme weather such as heat waves, heavy rains and wild fires.

rubric.why: The answer must connect increased carbon dioxide levels with global warming.
rubric.how: Explain that higher CO₂ levels lead to increased global warming.

rubric.why: Melting ice caps or warming oceans are stated consequences.
rubric.description: Give an effect on ice or oceans.
rubric.how: Mention melting ice caps or warming oceans.

rubric.why: Rising sea levels are an important ecosystem consequence named in the section.
rubric.description: State the effect on sea levels.
rubric.how: Explain that sea levels rise.

rubric.why: The section also links higher CO₂ levels with extreme weather.
rubric.description: Give an example of extreme weather.
rubric.how: Name a heat wave, heavy rain or wild fire.

modelAnswer: Higher levels of CO₂ lead to increased global warming.
Global warming can melt ice caps and warm oceans, causing sea levels to rise.
It can also cause extreme weather changes such as heat waves, heavy rains and wild fires.

written.text: Describe the harmful effects of the major pollutants present in the air.
written.finalAnswer: Carbon dioxide increases global warming, which can melt ice caps, warm oceans and raise sea levels, and can cause extreme weather. Carbon monoxide is poisonous and can cause suffocation and death by stopping red blood cells from carrying oxygen. NOₓ damages lungs, irritates eyes and damages vegetation; it can also cause acid rain. SOₓ irritates eyes, causes breathing difficulties and acid rain. Hydrocarbons can cause pneumonia, coughing and other breathing and lung diseases, and contribute to global warming. Particulate matter irritates eyes, causes severe breathing problems for people with asthma, dirties clothes and reduces visibility. Ozone can cause chest pain, coughing, throat irritation and congestion.

rubric.why: The answer should describe serious effects of the two carbon oxides.
rubric.description: Explain effects of carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide.
rubric.how: Give global warming effects for CO₂ and poisoning or oxygen-transport effects for CO.

rubric.why: Nitrogen oxides harm health and can contribute to acid rain.
rubric.how: Mention lung, eye or vegetation damage, or acid rain.

rubric.why: Sulphur oxides have both respiratory and environmental effects.
rubric.how: Mention eye irritation, breathing difficulties or acid rain.

rubric.why: Hydrocarbons and particulate matter also have harmful effects listed in the section.
rubric.description: Describe effects of hydrocarbons and particulates.
rubric.how: Give a breathing, lung, global-warming, eye or visibility effect.

rubric.why: The last mark is for correctly describing ozone's harmful effect.
rubric.how: Name chest pain, coughing, throat irritation or congestion caused by breathing ozone.

modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide: Higher levels increase global warming, which can melt ice caps, warm oceans and raise sea levels; extreme weather may also occur.
Carbon monoxide: It is extremely poisonous and can cause suffocation and death by stopping red blood cells from carrying the oxygen the body needs.
Oxides of nitrogen: They can damage lungs, irritate eyes and damage vegetation; they can also cause acid rain.
Oxides of sulphur: They irritate eyes, cause breathing difficulties and cause acid rain.
Hydrocarbons: They can cause pneumonia, coughing and other breathing and lung diseases; they also cause global warming.
Particulate matter: It irritates eyes, can cause severe breathing problems for people with asthma, makes clothes dirty and reduces visibility.
Ozone: Breathing ozone can cause chest pain, coughing, throat irritation and congestion.

written.text: Major Pakistani cities experience a very high AQI in winter which renders them the most polluted cities in the world. Point out some of the major causes of high AQI in these cities.
written.finalAnswer: Major causes include industrial pollution, vehicle emissions and crop burning. In winter, smoke mixes with fog to form smog, while nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, particulate matter and volatile organic compounds accumulate in the air.

rubric.why: Industrial pollution is one of the causes listed in the section.
rubric.how: Identify industrial pollution.

rubric.why: Vehicle emissions are one of the causes listed in the section.
rubric.how: Identify vehicle emissions.

rubric.why: Crop burning is also named as a cause of smog.
rubric.how: Identify crop burning.

rubric.why: The winter mixing of smoke and fog forms smog.
rubric.how: State that smoke mixes with fog to form smog.

rubric.why: These are the pollutants the section says accumulate in the air.
rubric.how: Give examples such as NOₓ, SO₂, particulate matter or volatile organic compounds.

modelAnswer: Industrial pollution, vehicle emissions and crop burning are major causes.
In winter, smoke in the atmosphere mixes with fog to form smog.
These factors contribute to the accumulation of nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, particulate matter and volatile organic compounds in the air.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for the definition of an air pollutant or ppm. Learn the textbook wording and the meaning of one ppm.
A constructed-response or descriptive question may ask for sources or harmful effects. Link each pollutant to an effect given in the table.
For a question about winter smog, state that smoke mixes with fog and name causes such as industrial pollution, vehicle emissions and crop burning.
For full marks, use pollutant names and explain the effect clearly; do not only list a general phrase such as “it is harmful.”

explain.title: Air pollutants
explain.body: Your textbook defines an air pollutant as: “Any substance (solid, liquid or gas) in the air which has adverse effect on human health and quality of life is called an air pollutant.” Remember that pollutants may be solids, liquids or gases.

explain.title: Concentration in ppm
explain.body: Your textbook says: “The concentration of a pollutant is expressed in parts per million (ppm). A concentration of one ppm means one part of pollutant per million part of solid, liquid or gas mixture in which the pollutant is formed.” In simple terms, ppm tells how much pollutant is present in a very large amount of mixture.

explain.title: Major sources and smog
explain.body: Burning fossil fuels is a major source of air pollution and releases gases and particles. The section describes winter smog as smoke in the atmosphere mixed with fog. Industrial pollution, vehicle emissions and crop burning contribute to it.

explain.title: Harmful effects
explain.body: Different pollutants have different effects. For example, carbon monoxide interferes with oxygen transport in blood, sulphur oxides can cause breathing difficulties and acid rain, and particulate matter can irritate the eyes and reduce visibility.

mistakes: Do not say that every air pollutant is a gas; the definition includes solids, liquids and gases.
Do not reverse the meaning of ppm: one ppm means one part of pollutant per million parts of the mixture.
Do not confuse smoke mixed with fog (smog) with the chemical process that forms ozone.
When asked how smog affects plants, include reduced carbon dioxide absorption during photosynthesis, not only “plants are harmed.”
Do not confuse the effects of carbon monoxide with those of carbon dioxide: CO is poisonous and interferes with oxygen transport; higher CO₂ levels increase global warming.
